newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses down, hit by interest rate fears.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses down, hit by interest rate fears.

text.p: European stocks fell on Thursday, distracted by interest rate worries and depressed over a poor opening on Wall Street after its record-breaking bull run.
On currency markets, the dollar was firm against the mark and stronger against the yen after Japanese authorities shut down a troubled bank, the first time they have done so in five decades.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, slipped as Wall Street fell quickly after its opening by 0.5 percent on profit-taking. It closed at 6,430.02 points on Wednesday, the 10th record this month.
Domestic issues had weighed heavily on bourses on this side of the Atlantic from the start of trading, decoupling them from the New York rally on Wednesday.
In London, stocks were down by 0.2 percent with many investors preoccupied by sterling's strength, interest rates and the possibility of unwelcome news in next week's budget.
The market feared that finance minister Kenneth Clarke might indulge in pre-election tax cuts in next Tuesday's budget despite rising inflationary pressures, analysts said.
"It would blow his credibility and the Bank of England would howl so I can't see it myself. But the uncertainty is enough to keep everyone flat in this market," another trader said.

Investors were still unsettled by British figures issued on Wednesday showing stronger-than-expected October retail sales, which reignited interest rate anxieties. The mood was not helped when figures on Thursday showed Britain's second quarter trade surplus was the best for 10 years.
"The data yesterday and today have encouraged people to anticipate a quarter-point rate rise before Christmas," one dealer said.
In Frankfurt, floor transactions ended in the minus column after listless trading which dealers said lacked direction. Computerised dealing on the IBIS DAX index was down in mid-afternoon.
French shares clawed back initial losses but volumes were thin. Dealers said the market trend was positive but Friday's monthly settlement could weigh on prices.
"No one has really any desire to buy ahead of the settlement," said one trader.

The dollar was stronger against the yen but underlying support for the Japanese currency came from Japan's robust September diffusion index of leading indicators which showed the economy was continuing to recover gradually.
Currency traders were keeping a close eye on Japan's banking sector after the closure of Hanwa Bank Ltd, suffocating under 190 billion yen ($1.7 billion) in problem loans.
The dollar also strengthened against the mark after the Bundesbank's policy-making council on Thursday decided to leave German interest rates unchanged.
While a rate change had not been expected, traders said markets had been marking time ahead of the Buba announcement.

On bullion markets, gold fell in London to $377.00 an ounce at the afternoon fix, its lowest since March 6, 1995. The metal had come under heavy selling pressure and was still vulnerable, dealers said.
Sentiment in the gold market has been increasingly gloomy in recent days since speculators were discouraged by the failure of a rally last week that peaked at just under $385 an ounce.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 111.35 yen and 1.4990 marks, compared with 111.17 yen and 1.4960 marks in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1545 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 7.9 points at 3,954.9.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 0.29 points at 2,233.10.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended down 2.16 points at 2,772.34.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternooin at $377.00 an ounce, compared to Wednesday's close of $379.15. Silver was down three cents at $4.93.
